summary: A 1931 offshore light on a concrete pier at the mouth of the St. Marys River, replacing the shore light at DeTour Point; now run by a preservation society with keeper stays.

lens.where: DeTour Passage Historical Museum, DeTour Village

access.note: Offshore, reached by boat; tours and keeper stays run by the preservation society.

events.note: Fresnel lens replaced with a modern optic
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places
Ownership transferred to DeTour Reef Light Preservation Society, 17 June 2010 per ACHP

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1847 date in the record belongs to the shore light at DeTour Point (established 1847, lit 1848); the present offshore station was lit 10 November 1931.

corrections.why: The present station was commissioned in 1931; 1847 is the earlier shore station at DeTour Point.

notes_for_editor: Moderate evidence: Bulletin 1931/1932, Lighthousefriends, USLHS roster, local/preservation sites. NRHP nomination not digitised. Bulletin 1932 OCR is poor, so the story paraphrases it. Roster disagreements: Lighthousefriends lists Ronald E. Freels as head keeper 1965 and Peter W. Day 1936; USLHS lists Freels under USCG and omits Day; Kurkierewicz is 1969-70 in USLHS but 1971-73 in Lighthousefriends; Hall 1931-1934 (USLHS) vs at least 1933. Cost $144,976 (LF) vs forecast $140,000 (Bulletin). The Michigan marker text reproduced on northernmichiganhistory.com says the 1861 tower was moved, but the Bulletin says only lens, lantern and watch room; not used. 1921 Commissioner rescue page not determined (point station). Story says 'Jones retired 1962 after 22 years' from LF; USLHS gives 1940-1962. The story text on keepers' heights (83 ft) from village/ACHP. Fact-check 2026-10-22: 1932 Bulletin figure '77 vessels per day' is printed as 'Average for 1919 season' in OCR; year dropped from story as unverifiable (PDF image not read). 1921 Commissioner entry OCRs the keeper as 'Sominer'; USLHS Detour Point roster (source 10) has Frank G. Sommer 1911-1925. Point tower height: LF 57 ft vs village 65 ft.
